atlas-lt.0001: Fintech licences and bank service centres
atlas-lt.0006: All Lithuanian immigration, visa, residence permit and salary rules are consolidated from primary sources in visas_immigration/lithuania/lithuania_visas_immigration_guide.md.
atlas-lt.0007: At the end of 2025, 248 fintech companies operated in Lithuania with about 7,800 employees; 231 of them were in Vilnius, and Lithuania ranks first in the EU by fintech licences issued.
atlas-lt.0008: Lithuania’s business-service centres employ more than 27,000 people in 100 companies, 37% of them for US-headquartered organisations and 36% in tech roles; brands include Danske Bank, Nasdaq, Western Union, SEB and Moody’s.
atlas-lt.0009: Lithuania’s second city for information-and-communication jobs
atlas-lt.0012: Eurostat counts 278,880 people in work in the Kaunas metropolitan region in 2021: 9,890 in information and communication (second in Lithuania, after Vilnius) and 2,560 in finance and insurance. The region’s GDP was €11.7 billion in 2021.
atlas-lt.0013: A small market centred on Vilnius, which has about two-thirds of the country’s ICT jobs and nearly three-quarters of its finance jobs: fintech, where Lithuania issues more licences than any other EU country, and business-service centres for Nordic banks and US firms. Non-EU graduates can stay 12 months to look for work, but rules for students were tightened in May 2026.
atlas-lt.0014: Tax, recruiting calendars, graduate programmes and language requirements were not researched; pay is Statistics Lithuania’s averages by sector and place, not entry pay.
atlas-lt.0015: Non-Lithuanian-speaking graduates’ prospects outside the business-service and fintech sectors were not measured; the Startup Genome and GFCI results for Kaunas and Vilnius are bands or associate-centre listings, not ranks.
atlas-lt.0017: second-hand marketplace, more than 2,000 staff, headquarters in Lithuania
atlas-lt.0018: cybersecurity and privacy products, headquarters in Vilnius
atlas-lt.0019: office in Kaunas as well as the Vilnius headquarters
atlas-lt.0020: the country’s largest provider of engineers
atlas-lt.0021: Eurostat counts 33,980 people employed in information and communication in the Vilnius metropolitan region in 2021, 67% of Lithuania’s 50,860, and 22,380 in finance and insurance, 73% of 30,530.
atlas-lt.0022: In 2025 ICT specialists were 5.7% of employment in Lithuania (83,100 people), against 5.0% in the EU.
atlas-lt.0023: In 2025 the average gross monthly wage in Lithuania was €2,411, €4,168 in information and communication and €3,848 in finance and insurance; in Vilnius County the three figures were €2,656, €4,359 and €3,997, and in Kaunas County €2,416, €3,715 and €3,362.
atlas-lt.0024: Swedbank AB gives its address as Konstitucijos pr. 20A, Vilnius.
atlas-lt.0025: Vinted says more than 2,000 people work from its headquarters in Lithuania and offices across Europe; its careers page lists roles in Vilnius and other Lithuanian locations.
atlas-lt.0026: Nord Security’s careers page speaks of its Vilnius headquarters and lists offices in Vilnius, Kaunas and Madrid.
atlas-lt.0027: Startup Genome’s 2026 report puts the Vilnius ecosystem’s value at $8 billion, against a European average of $14.3 billion.
atlas-lt.0028: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) lists Vilnius (34 assessments) and Kaunas (15) only as associate centres, too few assessments for a rank.
atlas-lt.0029: Vilnius University ranks 465th in the QS World University Rankings 2027, the highest of any Lithuanian university.
atlas-lt.0030: Invest Lithuania describes Kaunas University of Technology as the largest provider of qualified engineers in the country and Kaunas’ free economic zone as a hub of logistics and advanced manufacturing; 36% of Kaunas’ 50,000 students study engineering, manufacturing and construction.
atlas-lt.0031: In 2025, 92.7% of Lithuanian tertiary graduates aged 20–34 who finished within the last three years were in work (EU 85.3%), unemployment among 15-to-24-year-olds was 14.1% (EU 15.2%), and 60.8% of 25-to-34-year-olds had a tertiary degree (EU 44.8%).
atlas-lt.0032: Invest Lithuania reports that 58% of Lithuanian fintechs employ international staff in their Lithuanian offices, so fintech and service-centre work is possible in English.
atlas-lt.0033: The bank and Big Four postings read for Vilnius ask for Lithuanian as well as English: a Luminor graduate programme (fluent English and Lithuanian), an EY audit internship (English and Lithuanian) and a KPMG Baltics internship (fluent Lithuanian and effective English).
atlas-lt.0034: Swedbank’s Kick Start traineeships in the Baltic countries are open all year, and the bank is actively hiring trainees and junior specialists from February to May.
atlas-lt.0035: Vilnius University’s student-run VU Career Days ran from 23 to 27 March 2026, with the career fair and quick job interviews on 24 and 25 March and more than 70 companies.
atlas-lt.0036: The Vilnius Tech Career Day, now in its 23rd year, promotes registration for the 2027 edition; its page gives no date.
atlas-lt.0037: Vilnius hires graduates mainly into its fintech firms and global service centres: 248 fintech companies employed about 7,800 people at the end of 2025 (231 of them in Vilnius), and the business-service centres employ more than 27,000, many in jobs that are advertised in English. Banks and the Big Four also recruit, but their postings usually ask for Lithuanian as well.
atlas-lt.0039: Fintechs are the growth door: 77% of them plan to expand their teams in 2026, 58% already employ international staff in their Lithuanian offices, and the sector counts about 14,000 compliance and risk specialists. The business-service centres employ more than 27,000, 36% of them in tech roles.
atlas-lt.0040: Revolut, Shift4 (its largest European tech centre is in Vilnius) and Western Union, SEB and Nasdaq are among the names Invest Lithuania lists; SEB’s Vilnius centre said in 2016 that it recruits social-science graduates and students every year.
atlas-lt.0042: Swedbank’s Kick Start takes around 200 trainees a year across the Baltic countries, hires most actively from February to May, and offers a fixed-term contract at €1,200–1,800 gross a month in Lithuania. A Luminor 12-month graduate programme in corporate banking in Vilnius (a 2023 posting) paid €1,900 gross and asked for fluent English and Lithuanian.
atlas-lt.0043: Paid internships at the Big Four and tech teams
atlas-lt.0044: Internship adverts show the going rate and the language: an EY audit internship in Vilnius paid €1,100 gross a month and listed English and Lithuanian (the advert expired in December 2024), and a KPMG Baltics ERP internship paid €1,153 gross a month and asked for fluent Lithuanian and effective English.
atlas-lt.0045: The KTU WANTed platform lists internships by faculty with a paid or unpaid flag and the number of places, which makes it a good place to see how many are unpaid.
atlas-lt.0047: Vilnius University’s student-run VU Career Days ran from 23 to 27 March 2026 with more than 70 companies, a career fair and quick job interviews on 24 and 25 March; the Vilnius Tech Career Day is in its 23rd year with 100 participating organisations and more than 10,000 visitors, and registration for the 2027 edition is open.
atlas-lt.0048: State-funded internships for international students (2024 round)
atlas-lt.0049: The UPinLT programme paid international students and recent graduates €650 a month for additional internships at Lithuanian organisations; the Vilnius University round ran from 1 February to 31 August 2024. A later Vilnius University scholarship of €650 a month for a two-month internship in 2026, for final-year master’s students, had closed its applications by October 2026.
atlas-lt.0050: Under the 22 May 2026 amendments as the library’s visa guide reads them, non-EU students with a study permit work without a separate work permit: first- and second-year bachelor’s students are capped at 20 hours a week, while master’s and PhD students can work 40.
atlas-lt.0052: The University of Magdeburg’s guide for interns says to use your network first and calls a speculative application to the local office you want to join fairly successful; with personal contacts the formal cover letter may be replaced by a phone call or an email, although online applications are becoming more common.
atlas-lt.0053: Open ads and job portals (the experienced hire)
atlas-lt.0054: CVbankas listed 8,828 offers on 8 October 2026 (with pay ranges shown, a working-time filter for internships and popular searches for “no experience”, “internship” and “for students”); CV-Online listed 1,803 job ads, 958 of them in Vilnius and 14 internships; CV.lt shows the newest ads with no student section.
atlas-lt.0055: Lithuania is a small market that follows the financial and tech cycle: in 2025, 92.7% of recent graduates were in work (EU 85.3%) while youth unemployment was 14.1%, so the door is open for graduates but narrow for school-leavers.
atlas-lt.0056: Banks’ operations centres (SEB, Swedbank, Luminor) and the fintechs licensed in Vilnius, Revolut among them, hire graduates into compliance, risk and operations; the sector counts about 14,000 compliance and risk specialists. The bank programmes we read asked for Lithuanian as well as English.
atlas-lt.0057: Audit and accounting interns at EY and KPMG are advertised at about €1,100 to €1,150 gross a month, with Lithuanian and English both listed.
atlas-lt.0058: The country counts around 78,000 ICT specialists, and nine dedicated fintech study pathways run across universities and colleges; Shift4’s Vilnius office is its largest European tech centre.
atlas-lt.0059: Nord Security, founded in Vilnius, became Lithuania’s second unicorn in April 2022; we found no graduate-programme page for it.
atlas-lt.0060: Vilnius University and Vilnius Tech run the two large career events in the capital, and the Kaunas University of Technology runs the WANTed internship platform; employers recruit from all three through fairs and faculty postings.
